chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

that he looked at one of his companions, and upon him was a black sandal, so he said: 'What is your reason for the black sandal? Do you not know that it harms the vision, and it slackens the manhood, and it is more expensive in price than others, and none wear it except he swaggers (pompously) in it.'
ai.seo_question: What are the benefits and drawbacks of wearing black sandals according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) critiques the wearing of black sandals (*na'l*) by citing four specific drawbacks: potential harm to eyesight, weakening of virility, higher cost, and the wearer's tendency to swagger (*ikhtilal*). This reflects the Shia scholarly tradition of linking aesthetic choices to both physical health and spiritual humility, warning against vanity and extravagance in daily attire. The emphasis on 'swagger' highlights how external appearance can influence internal character and social perception.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from the one who mentioned it,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having looked at one of his<sup>asws</sup> companions, and upon him was a black sandal, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘What have you to do with the black sandals. Do you not know that it is harmful for the vision, and it slackens the manhood, and it is of a more expensive price than others, and none wear it except he swaggers (pompously) in it’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Mahbub from those whom he has mentioned who has said the following: “Once abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, looked at one of his people who wore a black shoe. He (the Imam) said, ‘What have you to do with a black shoe, did you not know that it is harmful to the eyes, it slackens the penis, besides it is more expensive than others and whoever wears it, he shows arrogance in it?”’
